abstract: Pluripotent cells of the early preimplantation embryo originate all types of somatic cell and germ cells of the adult organism. Permanent pluripotent cell lines (ES and EG cells) that were derived from an inner cell mass of blastocysts and primordial germ cells have a high proliferative potential and ability to differentiate in vitro into a wide variety of somatic and extraembryonic tissues as well as germ cells and to contribute to different organs of chimeric animals. In some cases pluripotent cells and primordial germ cells can generate teratomas, teratocarsinomas and some kinds of seminomas as the results of damages of differentiation programme of these cells. Experimental teratomas which formed after transplantation of undifferentiated ES and EG cells into immunocompromiced mice may provide a unique opportunity to study pluripotent cell specification and to develop novel approaches in carcinogenesis investigations. Research of signaling and metabolic pathways regulating the pluripotent cell maintenance and their multilineage differentiation are essential to search molecular targets to eliminate undifferentiated cells in tumors. Analysis of interactions between pluripotent cells and differentiated cells of the recipient animals, identification of the factors that may drive differentiation ES and EG cells in vivo contribute in understanding the mechanisms involved in the determination of cell fate during normal development and tumorigenesis. These data are important for development of effective and safe stem cell based technologies for prospective clinical treatment.
abstract_ja: 初期着床前胚の多能性細胞は、成体のすべての体細胞および胚細胞の起源となります。胚盤胞の内細胞塊と原始胚細胞に由来する永続的な多能性細胞株(ES細胞およびEG細胞)は、高い増殖能を持ち、in vitroで多様な体細胞および胚外組織、さらに胚細胞へ分化し、キメラ動物の様々な臓器に寄与します。多能性細胞や原始胚細胞は、分化プログラムに障害が生じた場合に奇形腫、奇形癌、そして一部のセミノーマを生じることがあります。未分化のES細胞およびEG細胞を免疫不全マウスに移植して生じる実験的奇形腫は、多能性細胞の運命決定を研究し、発がん研究に新たなアプローチを開発する独自の機会を提供します。多能性細胞の維持と多系列分化を制御するシグナル伝達経路や代謝経路の研究は、腫瘍中の未分化細胞を排除する分子標的の探索に不可欠です。多能性細胞と宿主の分化細胞との相互作用、およびES細胞やEG細胞のin vivo分化を促す因子の解析は、正常発生および腫瘍形成における細胞運命決定の機序の理解に役立ちます。これらのデータは、将来の臨床応用に向けた有効で安全な幹細胞治療技術の開発にとって重要です。
